description: Synthetic, hand-labeled user-conversation extraction corpus. v2 adds 16 cases (8 positive, 8 negative) to the original v1 16; thresholds unchanged. Every case is independent and contains no real user data.

cases.text: For future code reviews, I prefer concise feedback with one concrete test result.
I want you to run the relevant tests and explain important tradeoffs before you finish coding tasks.
I don't like hard-coded environment values; please make them configurable.
Actually, correction: I now prefer detailed review feedback rather than concise summaries. I changed my mind about this.
For the Orion project only, keep the public API backward compatible, even when a breaking redesign would be cleaner.
When debugging, show me the failing reproduction first, then the smallest fix and the verification result.
My goal this quarter is to reduce the build pipeline time below five minutes.
I maintain the Rust client and can review Rust lifetime and ownership changes myself.
Maybe a shorter answer would work here, but I haven't decided what format I prefer.
I don't have a preference about indentation in this repository.
I am not asking you to remember this and I do not want a lasting preference inferred from it.
My teammate prefers very short pull request descriptions, but I have not said what I prefer.
If I were leading the migration, I might choose a full rewrite; this is only a hypothetical.
I read an article about Kubernetes yesterday; I have no view on whether we should use it.
Would you prefer a table or a paragraph for this comparison?
For this one quick reply, just say yes or no; that is only for this message.
Please use bullet lists instead of long paragraphs when you summarize things for me.
I always want commit messages that explain why the change was made, not just what changed.
My goal for the next month is to migrate our billing service off the legacy queue.
In the Orion project specifically, never add new runtime dependencies without asking me first.
I'm the on-call owner for our Postgres clusters and I can handle replication failovers myself.
When you propose a refactor, list the files you would touch before changing anything.
Update: I used to want verbose logs, but now I prefer quiet logs with errors only. Please treat the new one as correct.

Which test runner would you pick for a small TypeScript library?
Suppose we had a bigger budget, I imagine I would hire two more engineers, but that's just daydreaming.
The vendor always wants invoices in PDF, which has nothing to do with my own habits.
For this single answer only, please use French; go back to normal afterwards.
Please forget this and do not save it anywhere: I sometimes like dark roast coffee.
